deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The previous page sets up the problem 'Ruhige Hinüberführung zu einem andern Gleichgewichtszustand'. A damped magnetometer needle is to be moved from rest at one equilibrium (0) to rest at a new one (1) with no residual swinging. T is the swing time and λ is half the Briggsian logarithmic decrement per swing. Phase is measured in quadrants R, so P = 2t/T and Q = 2t'/T. Gauss writes log10 p = -λP and log10 q = +λQ. His conditions are p cos P + q cos Q = 1 and p sin P = q sin Q (angles taken as P·90° and Q·90°).

Physical reading (mine): in phase-plane complex form the conditions say p e^{iP} + q e^{-iQ} = 1. This is the on–off–on manoeuvre: apply the new directing force (equilibrium at 1) for time t; remove it for time t'; the needle then arrives at a turning point exactly at 1; re-apply the force permanently.
- The undamped case (λ=0) gives p = q = 1 and P = Q = 60° = 2/3 quadrant, i.e. t = t' = T/3.
- The previous page solved the case 2λ = 0.081 by the law-of-cosines formulas cos P = (1+p²-q²)/2p and cos Q = (1+q²-p²)/2q. Result: P = 0.73554 R, Q = 0.59878 R, giving t = 15.30 s and t' = 12.45 s for T = 41.6 s.

THIS PAGE.
(a) Header '1837 Mai 12. Kraft von 4 pf. Stäben gemessen in G[ött.?]'. This is a small table of 'Kraft' (presumably magnetic moments) of bars A, C, 7, 34. There are two columns, headed 'Theod.' (theodolite) and 'Norell' (presumably an instrument or observer). The entries are 36.18/235.43, 30.62/298.16, 47.81/312.89, plus alternative values 310.77 and 305.38 (the last marked ':::' as doubtful). No computation is shown and the ratios are not constant, so no reconstruction is possible.

(b) 'Tafel': a table of P and Q (in quadrants) as functions of the argument 2λ.
- First attempt, 2λ = 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3: 5-place values. It starts at 2/3, 2/3 (undamped case).
- Beside it, 7-place values: 0.6666667/0.6666667, 0.7517015/0.5831232, 0.8362393/0.5030313, 0.9184135/0.4281209, 0.9967091/0.3597083.

(c) An abandoned inverse parametrisation (rows 0.5 … 1.0). My reading of the columns: argument x = q cos Q (equivalently 1 - p cos P); then y = p sin P = q sin Q; then log10 y; then P; then Q; then 2λ.
- Row x = 0.5: y = sin 60° = 0.8660254, log 9.9375307, P = Q = 0.6666667, 2λ = 0. This is the undamped case.
- Row x = 1.0: p cos P = 0, so P = 1 quadrant exactly and p = y. Then tan Q = y, q = √(1+y²), and λ = -log10 y = log10 q / Q. Solving gives y = 0.6278132 (log 9.7978304), Q = arctan(y)/(π/2) = 0.3569016 and 2λ = 2·0.2021696 = 0.4043392.
- The interior rows were left blank ('0,', '9.'). The point of this variant is that each row is solved for λ instead of for P, Q.

(d) Direct table at step 0.05 in 2λ from 0 to 0.45, giving P and Q to 7 places. The values agree with the 0.01-step table on the next page, which is labelled 'Durch Interpolation'. Examples:
- 0.05: 0.7091275, 0.6245802
- 0.20: 0.8362393, 0.5030313
- 0.45: 1.0340391, 0.3282193

(e) Extension to 2λ = 0.48, 0.52, 0.56, 0.60 to 10 places. The last five digits are written separately, with corrections above the crossed-out ones:
- 0.48: P = 1.0557942561, Q = 0.3102347068
- 0.52: P = 1.0840165471, Q = 0.2873312549
- 0.56: P = 1.1113161492, Q = 0.2656642913
- 0.60: P = 1.1376739026, Q = 0.2452268767
These round to the next-page entries.

(f) A scratch note gives Q(0.08) = 0.5996130 and Q(0.09) = 0.5913500. These are the bracketing values for interpolating at 2λ = 0.081, the case on the previous page. Linear interpolation gives P ≈ 0.73553 and Q ≈ 0.59879, matching the 0.73554 and 0.59878 found there. The isolated number '7253' is unexplained.

My spot check at 2λ = 0.2 (λ = 0.1): p = 10^-0.08362 = 0.82487 and q = 10^0.05030 = 1.12280. Then p cos 75.2615° + q cos 45.2728° = 0.20986 + 0.79016 ≈ 1.0000, and p sin = 0.79772 ≈ q sin = 0.79770. The table value therefore satisfies both conditions.
errors: First 7-place values for 2λ=0.1 (0.7517015, 0.5831232) are slightly wrong. They are corrected in the 0.05-step list to 0.7517085 and 0.5831198, consistent with the next page.

Coarse 5-place entries in the first table are off by one unit in the last place. For 2λ=0.3, 0.91842 should be 0.91841 (0.9184135) and 0.42811 should be 0.42812 (0.4281209). The overwriting suggests Gauss noticed this.
In the 2λ=0.25 row the last digits are overwritten; the final values per the next page are 0.8777253 and 0.4648355.
The inverse-parametrisation table (rows 0.5–1.0) is left incomplete. Only its two end rows are computed, and both are correct.

results.what: Conditions for transferring a damped oscillator (magnetometer needle) to a new equilibrium without residual oscillation by an on–off–on switching of the directing force. The conditions are p e^{iP} + q e^{-iQ} = 1 with log p = -λP and log q = λQ, solved numerically and tabulated against the logarithmic decrement.
results.modern_name: Zero-vibration bang-bang / on-off-on input shaping (posicast-type control) for a damped second-order system
results.usually_credited_to: O.J.M. Smith (posicast control, 1957); later input shaping (Singer & Seering, 1990)

results.what: Undamped special case: switching times t = t' = T/3 (60° of phase each)
Closed-form limiting row: P = 1 quadrant exactly when 2λ = 0.4043392, where y = p satisfies -log10 y = log10 sqrt(1+y^2)/(atan(y)/(pi/2)).
results.modern_name: Inverse parametrisation of a transcendental system (solve for the parameter instead of the unknowns)

results.what: Numerical table of P(2λ), Q(2λ) to 7–10 places, with subtabulation by interpolation

deep.surprise_reason: The page is essentially a numerical table. The underlying idea, though, is cancelling the oscillation of a damped needle by an on–off–on timed application of the force, solved exactly for arbitrary damping. That is a genuine 1837 anticipation of what control engineers call posicast or zero-vibration input shaping. Gauss and Weber are known to have devised practical calming (Beruhigung) procedures for magnetometers, so the physical idea is not entirely unknown as theirs. This exact damped-case solution and table, however, is a notable unpublished detail.

transcription_corrections: Header probably reads 'Kraft von 4 pf. Stäben gemessen in Gött.'. The final word is uncertain.
Row 0,1 of the first 7-place column reads 0.7517015 (with an overwritten digit), not a final value. The correct value 0.7517085 appears in the 0.05-step list.
Row 0.25: final values are 0.8777253 and 0.4648355 (overwritten digits), per the next page.
Bottom-right block: the extra five digits extend P and Q to 10 places. The crossed-out first entries for 0.48 are replaced by '42561' and '47068', giving 1.0557942561 and 0.3102347068.
Rows 0.5–1.0: the argument is x = q cos Q, not 2λ. The columns are p sin P, its log, P, Q and 2λ.
